panels.title: Floor Δ (15m avg)
panels.description:
Drift of the noise floor: mean floor over the last 15m minus the mean over the 15m before that.

Both sides are averaged on purpose. sdr_sweep_noise_floor_db is the median of ONE sweep, and the 30s scrape stores whichever sweep was last (~1 in 140 at 4.6 sweeps/s), so the raw series is heavy-tailed: p50 -51.1, p90 -48.3, p99 -44.0 dB over a typical day. A bare point-to-point 'x - x offset 15m' therefore exceeds ±4 dB ~12% of the time in BOTH directions — pure sampling noise, not drift — which pinned this tile red at random. Averaging keeps genuine drift (the real 2 dB evening step-down still reads 2.4) while holding sampling noise under the yellow threshold.

panels.title: Sweeps summarized per window
panels.description: How many sweeps the windowed aggregates are built from. Normal is rate(sdr_sweep_sweeps_total[5m]) x sdr_sweep_window_seconds (~277 at 4.6 sweeps/s over 60s). A live process reading 0 means capture wedged WITHOUT closing the pipe — the one failure mode --exit-on-eof cannot catch, and the sweep counter cannot show.

panels.title: B210 on bus
panels.description:
Is a USRP B2xx enumerated on the SDR host's USB bus at all (sysfs, independent of UHD).

If this is ABSENT the sweep data is stale or fabricated by a wedged capture — check here before believing anything else on this dashboard.

panels.title: USB link
panels.description:
Negotiated USB link speed of the B210.

WHY THIS MATTERS: the B210 enumerates at 480 Mbit/s and only negotiates 5000 once UHD initialises it. If it ever comes back at USB 2 the capture keeps running but throughput collapses and every sweep silently degrades — there is no other signal for that. A gap in the graph means the device left the bus entirely.

such hosts have a history of the xHCI controller wedging hard enough to lock the CPU, which needs a COLD power drain, not a reboot.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description:
Hottest hwmon sensor on the SDR host (CPU / NVMe / DIMMs).

Deliberately a max() rather than a specific chip: the useful question on a box with a history of spontaneous hard locks is 'is anything in here cooking', and max() survives hwmon renumbering.

panels.title: Clip / overload (ADC saturation — 60s mean duty is the health signal; per-sweep max = worst single sweep)
Clip fraction over time
panels.description: The health signal is the emphasised 'clip (60s mean)' trace — the duty cycle — which sits near the floor (~0.1%). The dim grey 'clip (60s max)' line is the single worst sweep in each 60s window; it rides high (~80%) BY DESIGN because a nearby duty-cycled transmitter keys up ~once a minute, so every window catches one railed sweep. It is de-emphasised (thin grey, no fill) on purpose — it is a reference, not an alarm. _max is the worst sweep in the window, _mean the average across all of them. The latest-sweep series is kept alongside the windowed one on purpose: _max/_mean only start at the 2026-07-22 exporter deploy, so dropping the original would blank this chart's earlier history.

panels.title: Clip duty (60s mean)
panels.description: Duty cycle — the mean fraction of ADC samples clipping (|IQ|>=0.99) across every sweep in the rolling 60s window (sdr_sweep_window_seconds). This is the health signal for overload: sustained values here mean real, continuous overdrive. Brief in-band bursts (e.g. a nearby duty-cycled transmitter keying up at <1% duty) drive the per-sweep MAX to ~0.8 while this mean stays near zero — that max trace lives on the 'Clip fraction over time' panel. The clip metric is compressive: on a constant-envelope chirp a per-sweep 0.8 is only ~2-3 dB of overdrive, not a railed ADC. Green < 1%, red > 5%.
